newsitem.title: POLAND: Bullish zloty up vs basket, one-day depos lower.
newsitem.headline: Bullish zloty up vs basket, one-day depos lower.

text.p: The Polish zloty strenghtened to a new high against the basket of currencies in live morning trade, despite the dollar's jump on world markets, fuelled by foreign capital investment, dealers said.

They said the upward pressure on the zloty on Friday was more likely coming from foreign demand for Polish stocks on the rising Warsaw bourse than for treasury paper, as early trade on the secondary T-bill and bond markets was slow.
"There is foreign investment into Polish stocks and this must have influenced the dollar/zloty rate," said Piotr Nowak from BPH SA.

At 0930 GMT the zloty was quoted at 3.81/3.71 percent from the trading band centre, up from opening's 3.60/3.50 percent. It was at 2.9051/70 to the dollar, up from opening's 2.9100/30 and at 1.8140/50 to the mark, up from 1.8175/95.

Polish shares were seen setting their seventh 33-month high this month. The main market's WIG index rose 300.8 points, or 1.9 percent yesterday to 15.846.7 and the parallel market's WIRR rose 1.4 percent to 2.812.4.
Some dealers saw a weak zloty resistance at 3.8 percent from the parity rate, but were also wary of central bank action against the zloty, which so far did not materialise.
"The NBP may intervene at any level now," said Przemyslaw Ciszecki from ING Bank.

Dealers said exporters were especially active selling marks whenver the German currency made any headway against the zloty in stop-loss transactions after the mark/zloty rate dropped to 1.8200 on Thursday's fixing from 1.8520 on January 2.
"I expect the NBP might step in to support the mark/zloty rate, because its deep fall has hard hit exporters," said Tomasz Zysko from BDK SA. @
The central bank offered to drain 100 million zlotys off the market for 14 days and offered to sell 100 million zlotys of 91-day NBP-bills and 200 million of 182-day NBP-bills.
At 0945 GMT overnight rates were quoted at 21.45/21.60 percent against opening's 21.35/21.65 percent, tomorrow/next rates were at 21.35/21.50 percent against 21.40/21.50 percent.
